h.activity.0: Even a little movement rather than none brings benefits.
h.activity.4: Beyond 300 minutes the guidelines indicate additional benefits.
h.activity.base: The WHO recommends 150-300 minutes a week of moderate activity, or 75-150 of vigorous activity. Here a minute in the Threshold or Maximal zone counts double, as in the guidelines. The estimate is based on heart rate, so strength exercises with rests are only partly counted.
h.activity.title: Moderate-to-vigorous activity
h.efficiency.base: It is the share of time in bed spent asleep; the reference is at least 85%.
h.efficiency.title: Sleep efficiency
h.latency.base: Falling asleep within 30 minutes is the reference.
h.latency.title: Time to fall asleep
h.rhr.0: If it stays above 90 bpm for several days, talk to your doctor.
h.rhr.1: Regular aerobic training is the most effective way to lower it.
h.rhr.base: In the meta-analysis of 1.2 million people, every 10 extra beats at rest were associated with a 9% higher mortality risk.
h.rhr.estimated: Some values are estimated from the lowest heart rates of the day, usually during sleep, so they may be a few beats lower than an awake measurement.
h.rhr.title: Resting heart rate
h.sleep.0: Regularly sleeping less than 6 hours is the first thing worth working on, also for recovery from training.
h.sleep.base: In the meta-analysis of 1.4 million people the lowest risk is at about 7 hours: short sleep is associated with 12% higher mortality and long sleep with 30% (associations, not causation). Wrist bands measure duration well but tend to overestimate it.
h.sleep.title: Sleep duration
h.sleep_weak: The band recognises quiet wakefulness poorly (35% in an independent study of a similar device): the value is indicative. Thresholds come from a consensus with conflicts of interest, flagged because there is no independent alternative.
h.steps.0: Adding even 2,000-3,000 steps a day brings the largest benefit.
h.steps.2: Moving towards 8,000 steps takes you to where the largest benefit begins.
h.steps.base: In the meta-analysis of 15 cohorts (47,471 adults), people taking about 10,900 steps a day had a 53% lower risk of death than those taking about 3,500; under age 60 the benefit levels off between 8,000 and 10,000 steps. Activities without steps (for example cycling or skipping rope) are not counted as steps.
h.steps.title: Steps per day
h.strength.1: One more a week is enough to meet the guidelines.
h.strength.base: The WHO recommends strength exercises for all major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week. In the meta-analysis of 16 cohorts the lowest mortality risk (-17%) was seen at about 40 minutes a week of strength training, with very low certainty evidence. In the last 7 days: {min:0} minutes.
h.strength.title: Days with strength exercises
h.waso.base: After falling asleep, being awake for 20 minutes or less in total is the reference.
h.waso.title: Minutes awake during the night

nc.carbs.text: EFSA indicates 45-60% of calories from carbohydrates for adults. Recovery between two close workouts has a separate box.
nc.energy.balanced.text: Without a deficit above 500 kcal a day, strength training can build lean mass (Murphy and Koehler 2022).
nc.energy.deficit_over.text: In the Murphy and Koehler 2022 meta-regression a deficit of about 500 kcal a day cancels the lean mass gains of strength training, while strength keeps improving: to preserve lean mass it is better not to exceed it.
nc.energy.moderate_deficit.text: Deficit within 500 kcal a day: according to Murphy and Koehler 2022 it is compatible with lean mass gains while you train.
nc.energy.no_deficit.text: Losing fat requires a deficit: with the logged intake and estimated expenditure you are even or in surplus.
nc.energy.surplus.text: With the logged intake and estimated expenditure you are in surplus: over time weight tends to rise.
nc.fat.text: EFSA indicates 20-35% of calories from fat. The WHO suggests not exceeding 30%, with a conditional recommendation (weaker evidence).
nc.fiber.text: At least 25 g a day for adults: strong WHO recommendation (2023), the same amount indicated by EFSA.

nc.missing_foods.one: The value is missing for {names:list}: the total is a minimum.
nc.missing_foods.other: The value is missing for {names:list} and others: the total is a minimum.

nc.protein.below_efsa_text: Below the amount that covers the needs of almost all adults (EFSA PRI: 0.83 g per kg, {efsa:0} g for you).
nc.protein.lose_fat.low: In a deficit, people who do strength training lose less lean mass with more protein: in the Refalo 2025 meta-regression the relationship is linear and at 1.9 g/kg the average loss reaches zero. Exploratory results and authors with ties to coaching companies: flagged reference.
nc.protein.lose_fat.ok: At least 1.9 g/kg: in the Refalo 2025 meta-regression lean mass in a deficit does not drop on average (reference flagged for conflicts of interest).
nc.protein.maintain.low: With strength training, above about 1.6 g/kg the Morton 2018 meta-analysis finds no further lean mass gains; below it, the gain is smaller. One author received funding from the National Dairy Council: flagged reference.
nc.protein.maintain.ok: At least 1.6 g/kg: above this amount Morton 2018 finds no further lean mass gains (reference flagged for conflicts of interest).

note.pai: PAI comes from studies by the group that invented it, which holds shares in the company licensing it: there are no independent checks. For the activity goal the WHO guideline applies (zone minutes).
note.zepp: Computed by the band with an unpublished method and no independent validation: it is a manufacturer figure, not a verified measurement. The only close independent study (a Mi Band 5 against polysomnography) recognised wake in only 35% of cases.
nut.athlete_text: {load} load ({min:0} min of training): {lo}-{hi} g of carbohydrates per kg a day, that is {glo:0}-{ghi:0} g for you. It is a position stand of scientific societies, not a meta-analysis, aimed at performance and not weight loss; one author had ties to the Gatorade Sports Science Institute. For this reason it remains a reference and does not trigger alerts.

nut.method_text: Kcal and nutrients from the label. The range uses the tolerances allowed by the European Union between label and actual content; calorie shares use EU factors (4 kcal per gram of carbohydrates and protein, 9 for fat, 2 for fibre). Expenditure is the one estimated by the band: a day enters the balance only if complete and with at least 20 hours of wear. An alert is certain when the whole range exceeds the threshold, otherwise probable.

In the studies the average dose was about 1 g per kg per hour ({g:0} g per hour for you), but the best dose has not been established.

rule.baseline.text: A single night varies a lot. As in the Australian Institute of Sport guidelines, the average of the last 7 days (at least 3 measurements) is compared with your norm over the last 60 days, plus or minus half of your usual variability. For HRV the logarithm is used, as in the studies.
rule.baseline.title: Resting heart rate and HRV: comparison with your norm
rule.hr_spike.text: A minute at least 25 bpm above both neighbouring minutes, with no steps or movement to explain it, or 25 bpm below (loss of sensor contact), is discarded. Increases during exertion stay: optical sensors err mostly during movement and their average accuracy is within 10%.
rule.hr_spike.title: Heart rate: one-minute spikes and drops
rule.spo2_min.text: The minimum is the lowest level held by two consecutive readings. An isolated reading at least 3 points below that minimum is within the error of wrist sensors (up to 4 points) and, with one measurement every 5 minutes, cannot be told apart from a true desaturation, which the AASM says must be measured continuously: it is counted as an isolated dip, not hidden. A dip lasting several readings stays in the minimum.
rule.spo2_min.title: SpO₂: confirmed minimum
rule.spo2_motion.text: Readings taken while you walk or move your wrist are discarded: at the wrist motion artefacts are more frequent than at the finger.
rule.spo2_motion.title: SpO₂: readings taken while moving

src.acsm_nutr.note: Position statement of scientific societies, not a meta-analysis; one author sat on the Gatorade Sports Science Institute expert panel (2014-2016, fee to the institution).
src.acsm_nutr.what: position of ACSM, Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and Dietitians of Canada on nutrition and performance
src.acsm_nutr.why: Shown only as a reference for carbohydrate doses for athletes: it does not trigger warnings.
src.ais_hrv.note: Authors from Australian public sports institutes.
src.ais_hrv.what: guidelines for HRV and resting heart rate
src.bent.note: Academic study (Duke) across several brands; the declaration was not readable.
src.bent.what: sources of error in optical heart rate sensors
src.bittencourt.note: Brazilian public funds (FAPESP, CNPq, CAPES); no conflicts.
src.bittencourt.what: HRV-guided strength training, no difference from a fixed plan
src.cappuccio.note: No funding; "not supported by industry", no conflicts declared.
src.cappuccio.what: sleep duration and mortality, meta-analysis (1.4 million people)
src.chaput.note: Part of the Canadian 24-hour movement guidelines; declaration not read.
src.chaput.what: sleep timing and regularity and health, review of 41 studies
src.compendium.note: Academic and free to use; the declaration was not readable.
src.compendium.what: Compendium of Physical Activities (MET values from 701 studies)
src.concheiro.note: Spanish public funds; no conflicts. It is the independent study closest to Zepp bands.
src.concheiro.what: Xiaomi Mi Band 5 versus polysomnography (wake recognised in 35% of cases)
src.craven.note: No funding; the authors declare no conflicts of interest.
src.craven.what: carbohydrates and glycogen recovery in 8 hours, meta-analysis of 29 trials
src.drain.note: Deakin University and Australian defence; declaration not read.
src.drain.what: Pandolf underestimates backpack load cost by 12-33%
src.efsa_cho.note: Public agency of the European Union; experts publish checked declarations of interests.
src.efsa_cho.what: reference values for carbohydrates (45-60% of calories) and fibre (25 g per day)
src.efsa_fat.note: Public agency of the European Union; experts publish checked declarations of interests.
src.efsa_fat.what: reference values for fat (20-35% of calories)
src.efsa_protein.note: Public agency of the European Union; experts publish checked declarations of interests.
src.efsa_protein.what: reference values for protein (PRI 0.83 g per kg per day in adults)
src.esco.note: University study of 109 men; declaration not read.
src.esco.what: independent check of the method (error ±7 mL/kg/min)
src.eu_kcal.note: European rule: 4 kcal per gram of carbohydrates and protein, 9 for fat, 2 for fibre, 2.4 for polyols, 7 for alcohol.

src.han.note: Chinese public foundations; no conflicts declared.

src.impellizzeri.note: No funding and no links with companies declared.

src.looney.note: Authors from the US Army research institute (public body); declaration not read.

src.mohoric.note: Slovenian Research Agency; no conflicts declared.

src.nsf_q.what: National Sleep Foundation sleep quality indicators

src.odriscoll.note: PhD at the University of Leeds; no conflicts declared. Devices tend to underestimate.
src.odriscoll.what: calories from wrist devices, meta-analysis of 60 studies
src.ohayon.note: Study not funded by companies, but authors with links to Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Sepracor and Cephalon.

src.paluch.note: Funded by the CDC (US public agency); no links with companies declared.
src.paluch.what: steps and mortality, meta-analysis of 15 cohorts (47,471 adults)
src.pandolf.note: US military laboratory, 1977; no declaration (not used at the time).

src.reynolds.note: University study (New Mexico); no company funding mentioned.
src.reynolds.what: estimating the 1RM from repetitions (no more than 10)
src.saeidifard.note: Authors from the Mayo Clinic (academic institution); the funding and conflicts declaration was not readable.

src.uth.note: Aarhus University and University of Southern Denmark; no declaration in the text.
src.vesterinen.note: Finnish Ministry of Education; no conflicts declared.

srcrm.buchheit.why: declaration not readable and roles in sports analytics companies: replaced by AIS 2023 and Vesterinen 2016
srcrm.edwards.why: the author founded a heart rate monitor company (Heart Zones): replaced by the Banister TRIMP
srcrm.frankenfield.why: review funded by a calorimeter manufacturer: replaced by Madden 2016
srcrm.iom_cho.what: at least 130 g of carbohydrates per day

srcrm.nsf_dur.why: foundation funded mostly by pharmaceutical and device companies: replaced by Cappuccio 2010

sri.text: Probability of being in the same state (asleep or awake) at the same time on consecutive days, from 0 to 100: 100 = identical times every day. In the review of 41 studies, more variable timing was associated with worse health outcomes, without a precise threshold: what counts is your trend. The band recognises quiet wakefulness poorly, so the value is indicative.

ui.foodSheet.values_per_100_g: Values per 100 g, as in the label table
ui.health.ratings_compare_values_thresho: The ratings compare your values with thresholds from guidelines and meta-analyses of large populations. They show where you stand; they are not a diagnosis: if you have doubts or symptoms, talk to your doctor.
ui.pickSheet.search_food_recipe_or: Search a food, a recipe or a saved meal
ui.profSheet.it_stays_only_this: It stays only on this device, in the app data. An empty field uses the Gadgetbridge value or the estimate shown.
ui.profSheet.weight_updated_from_weight: Weight is updated from the Weight card, with its date. Empty max HR: the higher of the age estimate (Tanaka 2001: 208 − 0.7 × age) and your peak of the last 2 years. Resting HR: the one measured by the band counts; this one is used only when it is missing. Basal metabolic rate: Mifflin-St Jeor (1990), from weight, height, age and sex. Empty stride: 0.415 × height.
ui.profile.calories_basal_metabolic_rate: Calories: basal metabolic rate with Mifflin-St Jeor (±10%). Active calories from heart rate with the heart rate reserve method above 40% of the reserve, otherwise from the cost of walking; strength, swimming and work with the Compendium values. Every estimate has a plausible range (±25%): in independent reviews fewer than one estimate in five stays within ±10%.
ui.profile.every_threshold_comes_from: Every threshold comes from meta-analyses, guidelines or independent studies. Funding and declared conflicts of interest are shown for each source; those linked to companies were replaced, or flagged when no independent alternative exists.
ui.profile.file_created_by_ritmo: The file is created by Ritmo and saved where you choose: no external service.
ui.profile.from_day_you_enter: From the day you enter it, the weight updates basal metabolic rate and calories; earlier days keep the weight of that time.
ui.profile.steps_activities_active_time: Steps, activities, active time, heart rate, HRV, stress, SpO₂ and PAI come from the band through Gadgetbridge. No data is sent to external services. The original values stay in the database; Ritmo only applies the cleaning described above.
ui.sheet.each_confirmation_teaches_ritmo: Each confirmation teaches Ritmo to recognise your workouts. Calories use the method suited to the type: Compendium 2024 for strength, swimming and work, Pandolf for walking with a backpack, heart rate (heart rate reserve) for running, rope and hiking. In strength training the added weight applies to the whole session: Compendium METs are per kg of body weight, so the added weight selects the code for resistance training and is not added to body weight. In confirmed strength and rope sessions jumps do not count as steps.
ui.sleep.stages_times_score_are: Stages, times and score are the ones computed by the band, as in the Zepp app. Stages measured at the wrist remain an estimate: compare them with yourself over time rather than with the references.

vit.text_hrv: An HRV lower than usual indicates incomplete recovery: in studies on HRV-guided training intensity is reduced until it returns to range.
vit.text_other: A night value outside your usual range can depend on illness, alcohol, heat or altitude. If it lasts several nights and you have symptoms, talk to a doctor.
vit.text_rhr: A resting heart rate higher than usual for a few days is associated with fatigue, little sleep, dehydration, alcohol or the onset of an illness.
vo2.altitude: At altitude: at {m:0} m ({name}) about {pct}% would remain ({lo}–{hi}%), that is {v:1} mL/kg/min.
vo2.altitude_extrap: At altitude: at {m:0} m ({name}) about {pct}% would remain ({lo}–{hi}%), that is {v:1} mL/kg/min: a value extrapolated beyond the 2,800 m measured, at high altitude the drop is probably larger.
vo2.hrmax_age: The maximum heart rate is estimated from age: with a measured one the error is smaller.
vo2.hrmax_observed: The maximum heart rate is the one observed in your workouts.
vo2.met: Each extra MET (3.5 mL/kg/min) is associated with a 12% lower mortality risk.
vo2.need_rest: 3 days with resting heart rate are needed
vo2.need_text: At least 3 days with the band's resting heart rate in the last 7 days are needed.
vo2.text: Estimate from the ratio of maximum to resting heart rate (15.3 × HRmax / resting HR). In the independent check the typical error is ±7 mL/kg/min: look mainly at the trend.
w.none: No value entered: the one from the profile or Gadgetbridge is used.
w.unavailable: Weight not available, try again shortly
wc.coherent: The weight trend is consistent with the logged balance: with the logged balance it should be between {elo:2} and {ehi:2} kg a week, your trend is {slope:2} kg a week ({slo:2} / {shi:2}).
wc.faster: Weight is falling faster than the balance explains: with the logged balance it should be between {elo:2} and {ehi:2} kg a week, your trend is {slope:2} kg a week ({slo:2} / {shi:2}). Perhaps you log more than you eat or burn more than estimated; at the start of a deficit you also lose water and glycogen.
wc.fat_energy: Fat is worth 39.5 MJ/kg (about 9,400 kcal): a true deficit of 500 kcal a day removes at least {kg:1} kg in 4 weeks.
wc.need: To compare weight with the balance you need at least {weighins} weigh-ins spread over {span} days or more (now {now_w}{now_span}) and {days} complete days wearing the band in the last 28 (now {now_d}).
wc.slower: Weight is falling less (or rising more) than the balance allows: with the logged balance it should be between {elo:2} and {ehi:2} kg a week, your trend is {slope:2} kg a week ({slo:2} / {shi:2}). The most common causes: unlogged foods or underestimated portions, estimated expenditure too high, or water and glycogen (after days with a lot of salt or carbohydrates).
